images.caption: Figure 1:BlenderWorldtaxonomy and examples. References are shown left/top and GPT-6-Astra results right/bottom.

Figure 2:Construction and rubric derivation pipeline inBlenderWorld.Illustrating the end-to-end workflow from diversified task and reference curation, application-grounded brief specification with dual-track validation, to multi-model verified and frozen binary rubrics.
Figure 4:Evaluation pipeline ofBlenderWorld. Structural and visual evidence support binary rubric decisions, which are fused with dimension scores.
Table 2:Performance on all 223BlenderWorldtasks.Models are ranked by mean fused Score; bold marks the best completion values.

view, (c) distorted lion-cub anatomy, (d) a reclining person floating above
the lawn.

Figure 12:Score components and fusion-weight sensitivity.(a) Paired scores for 2,899 outputs, with logarithmic bin counts.
(b) System ranks at five rubric weights; the main Score usesλ=0.5\lambda=0.5. All 223 tasks remain in each system mean.

Figure 13:Task-category scores for all thirteen systems.Cells show mean fused Score on each category’s fixed task subset, including
assigned zeros. Category sizes appear below the columns; cells are rounded
to the nearest integer.

Figure 15:Selected operations in three failure trajectories.(a) GPT-6-Astra maps reference people onto textured flat quads.
(b) GPT-5.6-Sol checks projection markers while the body remains unsupported.
(c) Opus-5 checks the combined leg-and-caster height in place of the
specified timber length. Images in (a) and (b) are archived renders;
the dimension bars in (c) are schematic.

Figure 16:Construction and verification across three typical workflows.Opus-5 is on the left and GPT-6-Astra on the right. Both booth outputs pass all
binary criteria. Both lion cub pipelines construct fur and rigging, yet their
dimension scores remain 37.50 and 53.75. The sofa reverses the ordering
across components: Opus-5 has higher Dimension (with better lighting), while GPT-6-Astra has higher
Rubric; Figure15c details the timber-length
error.

Figure 17:Construction and verification across another three workflows.Opus-5 is on the left and GPT-6-Astra on the right. Both systems use high-to-low
texture baking for the chest and construct two membrane leaflets, with
all binary criteria passing in both tasks. Their checks differ in the
train task: Opus-5 inspects axle/path parameterization, while GPT-6-Astra fits
the camera numerically. Both deliver 80-frame clips at 30 fps, but GPT-6-Astra
has higher frozen Rubric and Dimension scores. The frames show 0.00,
1.30, and 2.60 s.
